title: POC weekly sync - model selection and pinning (Enterprise Payments)

Customer requested a deeper security vetting and a short canary run on dedicated capacity.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recording/3f9b
Attendees: Sara Gomez (Redwood AE), Elliot Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Head of ML - Enterprise Payments), Omar Ruiz (Platform Eng), Lina Zhang (Security)

00:00 - Sara: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda — benchmark review, model pick, pinning/rollbacks, and next steps. Any changes?
00:08 - Maya: No, that's good. We mostly want to make sure the model choice meets our p95 SLO and cost targets.
00:14 - Elliot: Cool, I shared the spreadsheet pre-call; I'll walk through the latest numbers. Note: some auto-transcription munged the model names in the sheet — "Redwood v2 medium" listed as redwooD v2-med in one column, sorry about that.
00:28 - Elliot: Ok first slide — latency. Under our sample traffic (avg seq 120 tokens) Redwood-v2-medium (quantized int8) p50 is ~32ms p95 ~128ms on Dedicated A100 pool, cost about $0.0009/token equivalent; Mistral-like-open-7b p50 ~28ms p95 ~150ms but higher token usage for same prompt because of longer outputs, and the cheaper quantized fallback (4bit) adds ~15% variance and occasional decode artifacts.
01:01 - Omar: Wait, the p95 for Mistral was higher even though p50 was lower? Is that noise from batching?
01:06 - Elliot: Yep batching and KV cache warmup. We saw a lot of p95 spikes during short bursts; that's why I recommended pinning on Redwood-v2-medium and using Mistral-7b-quant4 as fallback for cost control.
01:20 - Maya: Can you explain pinning behavior again — what happens on rollback and how quickly we can flip to fallback?
01:26 - Elliot: Sure. Pinning means the route is locked to a specific model version. We'll set up a canary policy: 95% traffic to pinned model, 5% to fallback for validation for 24 hours. If p95 crosses threshold or errors > 0.5% we automatic rollback to fallback. Rollback is immediate at control-plane level, typically a few seconds for routing changes, but warm caches mean a brief latency blip for first requests.
01:51 - Lina: From security side we need a clear audit trail and access control for who triggers rollbacks; can we get RBAC on the console and audit logs per route? Also KMS integration for keys.
01:59 - Sara: Yes, RBAC and audit logs are part of our Private/Dedicated offering; we'll include logs link. Elliot, can you note that action?
02:06 - Elliot: noted. Also small transcription note — the sheet has a column labelled "KV cash" instead of KV cache, apologies, we meant key-value cache.
02:14 - Maya: Good catch. About cost — if we pin to Redwood-v2-medium what's the expected unit cost compared to hosted API?
02:22 - Elliot: On Dedicated it's about 20-30% cheaper per token vs hosted at our sample throughput due to amortized GPU utilization. But if you have lots of tail traffic, autoscale bursts can add cost. Fallback to quantized Mistral-4bit variant reduces cost by another ~40% at the expense of occasional regression in answer quality; we can tie quality monitoring to prompt test set to detect that.
02:46 - Omar: Are rollbacks manual or automatic only? We need manual override for ops to force rollback during incidents.
02:52 - Elliot: Both. Default is automatic thresholds but an ops user with RBAC can trigger manual rollback in console; we can set the escalation policy to notify teams.
03:01 - Maya: For the canary run, do you recommend Dedicated or Hosted? We prefer Dedicated to match production env but we are mindful of capacity.
03:08 - Elliot: Dedicated gives more deterministic latency; Hosted is faster to spin up. For this POC we suggest 24h canary on Dedicated but we'll keep a fallback to Hosted if capacity pressure arises.
03:19 - Sara: Ok next, data residency and encryption — Lina?
03:22 - Lina: We need the usual: SOC2 Type II, ISO, KMS with customer-managed keys for private deployment, and retention controls (30/90 days). Also a list of sub-processors. We'll send our questionnaire.
03:33 - Sara: We'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report after the call.
03:37 - Elliot: Quick note on monitoring: we'll push per-route dashboards for p50/p95, token cost, errors. We'll add a quality regression alert tied to a holdout prompt set you provided.
03:49 - Maya: That prompt set — we've updated it with a payments-specific QA set; I'll upload to the drive.
03:54 - Elliot: Great. Any objections to pinning to Redwood-v2-medium with quantized Mistral fallback?
03:59 - Maya: Sounds reasonable, want to see canary results first but agree in principle.
04:05 - Omar: And confirm we get ability to force rollback and the audit logs.
04:10 - Sara: Yes. Final recap: Redwood sends benchmark sheet + config, SE runs 24h dedicated canary with fallback and collects p50/p95 + token cost, customer reviews security docs + sends SLOs.
04:21 - Lina: I'll also add our minimal access controls and notify who can hit rollback.
04:25 - Sara: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the security deep dive. Thanks all.

End of transcript.
